# Mean return per period (`arithmetic_mean`)

*Category: Return summary · Nature: estimated · Unit: decimal_return · Formula id: `arithmetic_mean@v1` · Methodology 0.1.0*

## 1. What does it measure?

Average single-period return.

## 2. Formula

```text
(1/n) * sum(r_t)
```

## 3. Required inputs

Periodic simple returns.

## 4. Is higher or lower better?

Higher is better.

## 5. Plain-language interpretation

The typical return in one period (e.g. one month), ignoring compounding.

## 6. Professional interpretation

Sample mean; the numerator of Sharpe-type ratios. An estimate of the expected return with standard error roughly sigma / sqrt(n).

## 7. Assumptions

- Returns are identically distributed over the history.

## 8. When can it be misleading?

- Returns are volatile: the arithmetic mean overstates compounded growth.
- Few observations are available: sampling error dominates.

## 9. Minimum sensible data

One observation; low confidence below 3 years. (policy `location`: Mean-type estimates: low confidence below 3 years, moderate below 5 years.)
